pages.text: Once a scanner cell lights up, here is the usual plan: $(li)Go to the chunk and dig a $(item)1 x 1 shaft$() straight down to the bedrock layer. Look for fossilstone and crude oil near Y -60. $(li)Find a deposit block and note its $(item)X and Z$().

The pumpjack base must sit exactly above it. $(li)Fill the shaft from the deposit up with $(item)industrial pipes$(), with nothing else in between. One steel ingot gives $(item)8 pipes$() in a stonecutter, so a shaft from Y 64 needs about 16 ingots. $(li)Crude oil blocks in the shaft can simply be replaced by pipes.

Industrial pipes can be filled with liquid concrete and dry into $(item)concrete encased industrial pipes$(). They still count as a valid column, so you can seal the shaft for good. Broken, they give back a normal industrial pipe.$(br2)With the column built, put the pumpjack base on top of it at the surface. The next chapter explains the rest of the pumpjack.
